newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures ends lower as market consolidates.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures ends lower as market consolidates.

text.p: FCOJ futures settled narrowly mixed in thin dealings, as players sat out to assess the market's recent move higher.
September rose 0.15 on the day to finish at 123.40, having ranged from 124.00 to 123.00. November ended 0.70 lower at 117.70, while the remaining months closed 1.05 to 0.55 weaker.
Analysts said the charts point to higher near-term prices.
"We broke through downtrend channels, broke out of a bull flag, and the Sept/Dec switch is acting bullishly," said Bernard Savaiko, a senior analyst with Paine Webber.

He noted underlying support at current levels, and pegged resistance between 124.00 and 125.00 in September. Above that level the contract could encounter resistance in a gap between 128.00 and 128.00.
On the fundamental front, Hurricane Edouard appears poised to bypass the Caribbean but players continue to monitor the weather system, market sources said.

And expectations for strong U.S. production could keep a lid on prices. "It's not quite as high as many traders were anticipating but it's up from year-ago levels," Savaiko said. "It's hard to get wildly bullish about that."
The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its next estimate for the Florida crop in October.
September 3 is the first notice day, and September 10 the last trading day for the spot contract.
